chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever eats saffron deliberately, or food in which there is perfume, so upon him is blood (slaughter of an animal). So if it was due to forgetfulness, so there is nothing upon him, and he should seek Forgiveness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to the sacrificial animal (dam) penalty in Hajj jurisprudence
key_terms.زَعْفَرَاناً: Saffron, a spice often used in food and associated with fragrance

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for eating saffron or food with perfume while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between intentional and unintentional consumption of perfume in food while in Ihram, establishing 'dam' (slaughtering a sheep) as the expiation for deliberate acts. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on intentionality (niyyah) in determining liability, aligning with the broader principle that forgetfulness exempts one from punitive penalties, requiring only spiritual repentance.
